title: CENTCOM Disables a Cargo Ship in the Gulf of Oman, Iran Lifts Its Missile Range Cap, and European Troops Train in Poland for a Postwar Ukraine Force
subhead: US naval forces fired on and disabled a commercial vessel attempting to run the Iran blockade in the Gulf of Oman while the Pentagon stood up a new task force to interdict Tehran's overland weapons corridors. Within hours, Iran announced it had removed its self-imposed limit on ballistic missile ranges and claimed two oil tankers hit mines near Hormuz, while in Europe 2,800 troops from 11 nations prepared for a British- and French-led exercise in Poland to rehearse a postwar deployment to Ukraine.

sections.heading: US Disables Vessel in Gulf of Oman and Stands Up Land-Route Task Force
sections.body:
US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced that American military forces fired upon and disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman on Saturday after the ship ignored warnings and attempted to breach the naval blockade on Iran (AP News, The Hill, Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty). The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) confirmed a military incident involving a cargo ship off Oman, while US officials noted that 147 vessels have been redirected since maritime interdiction operations began (Anadolu Agency, Sabah).

Alongside the maritime action, the Pentagon launched a new task force specifically assigned to disrupt Iran's land-based supply routes used to move weapons and military equipment across the Middle East (Al Jazeera, CBS News). Meanwhile, the USS Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group (CVN-71) — accompanied by cruiser USS Chosin (CG-65) and destroyers USS Paul Hamilton (DDG-60) and USS Decatur (DDG-73) — pulled into Singapore on Friday for its final port call before joining two other US carrier strike groups in the Middle East (USNI News, The War Zone).
sections.whyItMatters: With a third carrier strike group days away from the Middle East and a new land-interdiction task force active, the Pentagon is shifting from coastal quarantine to a theater-wide containment operation.

sections.heading: Iran Lifts Missile Range Cap as IRGC Reports Two Tankers Hit Mines Near Hormuz
sections.body:
Iranian authorities announced on Saturday that Tehran has lifted its self-imposed 2,000-kilometer limit on ballistic missile ranges, with Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) spokesman Hossein Mohebbi stating that work to extend missile reach is proceeding without pause (AP News, Habertürk). The announcement comes days after a Financial Times report cited by M5 Dergi revealed Russian defense production schedules showing Iran ordered 90 missile launcher systems from Russian manufacturers in the 2024–2025 period.

In the Strait of Hormuz, the IRGC stated that two oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire after switching off their navigation systems and entering an unauthorized route, while the United Arab Emirates rescued 22 sailors and Iranian media reported explosions heard on Qeshm Island and in Jask, Sirik, and Bandar Abbas (Anadolu Agency, Al Jazeera). Across the Gulf, Saudi Arabia briefly activated civil defense warning sirens in Dhahran, Dammam, Al-Ahsa, and Abqaiq during clashes with Yemen's Houthis, while Yemeni government forces reported conducting over 800 operations that neutralized 130 Houthi fighters and destroyed 50 vehicles and missile launchers (Times of Israel, Anadolu Agency).
sections.whyItMatters: Removing the 2,000-kilometer range cap places capitals across central and western Europe within the theoretical envelope of future Iranian ballistic missile variants.

sections.heading: Britain and France Lead 11-Nation Exercise in Poland for Postwar Ukraine Force
sections.body:
Britain and France will lead 2,800 troops from 11 nations in a two-week military exercise in Poland designed to test how allied forces would move, protect, and supply a stabilization contingent deployed to rebuild Ukraine's military after a future ceasefire, according to Defense News. The drill comes as Spain prepares a new 437 million euro military aid package for Kyiv following talks between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez in Madrid (M5 Dergi).

Elsewhere on NATO's eastern flank, Denmark and Lithuania became the latest Baltic navies to sign contracts for Finland's 'Blocker' naval mines under a joint Finnish procurement scheme (Defense News). Meanwhile, US European Command (EUCOM) launched a theater-wide vigilance campaign instructing US troops, civilian staff, and family members across Europe to minimize their digital footprints and watch for suspicious activity amid rising hybrid threats (Defense News).

On the battlefield, Russian forces launched overnight drone and missile attacks that wounded nine people in Ukraine, while new footage confirmed Russian Mi-28NM attack helicopters are now firing low-cost jet-powered cruise missiles — assessed as S8000 Banderol or Dan-T munitions — and Russian state conglomerate Rostec unveiled a truck-mounted mobile version of its 30mm Tsitadel counter-drone air defense system (AP News, The War Zone, M5 Dergi).
sections.whyItMatters: European armies are rehearsing the logistics of a post-ceasefire deterrence force on the ground in Poland even as Russia fields standoff cruise missiles on attack helicopters to keep Ukrainian air defenses stretched.

sections.heading: Pentagon Awards $450M Golden Dome Contract, Weighs Pacific Airfields and Amphib Gap
sections.body:
The US Department of Defense awarded Viasat an indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract worth up to $450 million to design, field, and scale the Mission Operation Center for the Space Data Network Backbone supporting the Golden Dome satellite data relay network (Breaking Defense). Separately, the European Commission is expected by the end of November to select one of two competing industrial consortia to build a European hypersonic and ballistic missile interceptor demonstrator targeted for 2030 (Breaking Defense).

In the Indo-Pacific, the US Air Force is advancing plans to revive World War II-era airfields across three American Pacific islands to support more than 6,000 aircraft operations annually, while operational F-15EX Eagle II fighters have begun flying with conformal fuel tanks to extend range (Defense News, The War Zone). At the same time, US Marine Corps leadership warned that its amphibious warship fleet must grow from 31 to 40 vessels to meet global mission demands, and Sierra Nevada Corp detailed why it withdrew its clean-sheet Freedom Jet from the US Navy's T-45 jet trainer replacement competition, leaving a single bidder (The War Zone, Breaking Defense).

In Northeast Asia, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected an under-construction warship assessed as a 10,000-ton cruiser at the Nampho Shipyard — twice the displacement of Pyongyang's 5,000-ton destroyers — while satellite imagery analyzed by CSIS indicated China could launch its fourth aircraft carrier, the nuclear-powered Type 004, in 2027 (USNI News, M5 Dergi).
sections.whyItMatters: As China advances toward a nuclear-powered carrier and North Korea builds a 10,000-ton surface combatant, the US Air Force is dispersing across WWII island runways and adding fuel tanks to tactical fighters to survive long-range Pacific salvos.

sections.heading: Drone Strike Kills Three Colombian Soldiers During US-Colombia Joint Exercise
sections.body:
An explosive drone attack on a military base in Colombia killed at least three soldiers and seriously injured eight others on Saturday, the Colombian army reported (AP News, Anadolu Agency). The attack took place just days after hundreds of American and Colombian troops kicked off a large-scale bilateral military exercise in Colombia as part of the Pentagon's renewed operational focus on the Western Hemisphere (Defense News).

Simultaneously, the US Army unveiled its new MALET clip-on kit, which allows infantry soldiers to rapidly convert standard mortar rounds into drone-dropped munitions, while the French Navy conducted close-in defense drills against asymmetric drone and fast-boat threats aboard its newest combat supply ship FS Jacques Stosskopf (A726) in Toulon, and the UK and Italy completed the first internal weapons bay release of an MBDA Meteor beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile from an F-35B Lightning II (The War Zone, USNI News, M5 Dergi).
sections.whyItMatters: The lethal drone strike on a Colombian base during a US joint exercise shows that low-cost aerial munitions are no longer confined to Eastern Europe and the Middle East, forcing Western Hemisphere forces to adapt base defense immediately.

bottomLine: Saturday's operational tempo centered on the Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz, where US forces disabled a commercial ship attempting to breach the Iran blockade, the Pentagon created a task force to sever Iranian land supply corridors, and Tehran responded by lifting its 2,000-kilometer missile range limit while reporting two tankers hit by mines. In Europe, Britain and France are leading 2,800 troops from 11 countries in Poland to rehearse a postwar Ukraine deployment as Baltic navies buy Finnish naval mines and EUCOM warns personnel of hybrid threats. Meanwhile, the Pentagon committed up to $450 million to Viasat for its Golden Dome space relay network and moved to revive WWII Pacific airfields as USS Theodore Roosevelt reached Singapore en route to the Middle East.
sources: Breaking Defense, Defense News, USNI News, The War Zone, AP News, Al Jazeera, CBS News, The Hill, Times of Israel, Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty, UKMTO, CSIS, Anadolu Agency, SavunmaSanayiST, M5 Dergi
